details:
LUNA-OPS: Lunar Landing Site Navigator

The lunar south pole is one of the most challenging regions for future exploration. Unlike locations with a high Sun, the Sun remains close to the horizon, while Earth also appears at a low elevation. Crater rims and surrounding terrain can obstruct sunlight and direct communication with Earth. These conditions vary with both location and time, making landing-site analysis complex.

What does LUNA-OPS do?

LUNA-OPS is an interactive lunar landing-site analysis and mission-planning platform designed to help users explore candidate landing locations near the lunar south pole.

It uses NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation models and NASA/JPL SPICE ephemerides to calculate and visualize the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local terrain.

The platform brings several capabilities together:

  • 3D Lunar Exploration: Explore the Moon using an interactive 3D globe, select candidate locations and inspect local terrain.
  • Sunlight Analysis: Determine when a location receives sunlight, identify terrain obstructions, examine illumination windows and understand periods of darkness.
  • Earth Visibility Analysis: Calculate when Earth is directly visible above the local terrain horizon and explore visibility windows.
  • Operational Overlap: Identify periods when sunlight and direct-to-Earth visibility occur together.
  • Landing Site Assessment: Evaluate candidate lunar landing areas using terrain characteristics, slope, roughness, elevation, depression candidates and uncertainty data. Inspect landing footprints and identify potential terrain hazards through preliminary screening.
  • Terrain and Hazard Screening: Analyse elevation, slope, roughness, terrain coverage, height uncertainty, depression candidates and landing footprints.
  • Communication Analysis: Explore communication geometry and user-defined radio-frequency link-budget scenarios, including hypothetical relay configurations.
  • Site Comparison: Compare multiple candidate landing locations across sunlight, Earth visibility, terrain and operational parameters.

How does it work?

The Python scientific engine processes lunar terrain elevation data and planetary geometry using NASA/JPL SPICE information. FastAPI provides the calculated results through APIs, while the React-based frontend presents them through interactive maps, 3D visualizations, analysis panels and comparison views.

The application also provides Technical and Public modes, helping both technically experienced users and general audiences explore the results.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNA-OPS brings multiple lunar site-analysis capabilities into one integrated platform instead of requiring users to examine separate tools and datasets.

It helps users:

  • Understand how local terrain affects sunlight and Earth visibility.
  • Identify useful illumination and communication windows.
  • Explore terrain characteristics before selecting candidate landing locations.
  • Compare different sites using consistent analysis parameters.
  • Understand potential operational constraints through interactive visualizations.

Its intended impact is to support more informed exploration and preliminary planning for future lunar south-pole missions, making complex lunar environmental data easier to interpret and compare.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Backend: FastAPI
  • Frontend: React
  • Scientific Data: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA elevation models and terrain datasets from PGDA Products 78 and 90.
  • Planetary Geometry: NASA/JPL SPICE ephemerides and NAIF kernels and DE440 gravitational constants.
  • Reference Sources: NASA PDS illumination products, LROC WAC data, JPL Horizons and NASA GSFC Eclipse resources.
  • Visualization: Interactive 3D lunar globe, terrain maps, horizon visualizations and analytical dashboards

What makes LUNA-OPS creative?

The key innovation is bringing sunlight analysis, Earth visibility, terrain screening, communication geometry and multi-site comparison together in one interactive lunar planning environment.

Rather than treating sunlight and communication as simple independent measurements, LUNA-OPS considers the actual surrounding terrain and changing positions of the Sun and Earth. Users can explore how a change in location or time changes the visibility conditions and operational picture.

The platform also distinguishes calculated results, estimates, measured inputs and preliminary assessments, helping users understand the origin and meaning of the information presented.

Factors Considered

Our team considered local terrain elevation, crater-rim obstruction, solar illumination, Earth viewing geometry, time-dependent visibility, terrain slope, roughness, uncertainty, communication requirements and the differences between candidate landing locations.

LUNA-OPS is intended as a research and preliminary planning aid. It is not a certified landing-safety system, a NASA-approved recommendation system or a final mission decision tool.
